taxonomy.object: Five nonexclusive functional relations between a specified input change C and a concrete judgment J; not five trained classifiers, not mutually exclusive task IDs, and not a latent-reasoning oracle.

origin.context: Guide identifies the original user-provided 2026-09-07 scheme, conveyed during 09-08 work. The contribution should be described as proposing/operationalizing the study taxonomy; do not attribute invention of all five concepts to the writing agent.

rows.name: New support
rows.criterion: C supplies genuinely new evidence supporting a specified J; the same support must not already be present. Support need not uniquely determine the diagnosis.
rows.example: New expiratory wheeze supplies compatible support for Bronchitis.
rows.boundary: Adding compatible support is not diagnosis proof; an answer change or duplicated old fact alone is insufficient.

rows.name: Support withdrawal
rows.criterion: An identifiable basis for an earlier judgment is explicitly negated, invalidated or removed as a valid basis by C.
rows.example: Male-to-female demographic change removes one epidemiological support for Lesch-Nyhan, while other findings remain.
rows.boundary: Omitted information is not a clinically negative observation; removing one constraint does not remove all constraints or exclude the disease.

rows.name: Candidate reconsideration
rows.criterion: At least two identifiable candidates and evidence changing their relative support must be specified.
rows.example: Replacing a spontaneous-pneumothorax history with DVT history changes relative support for pneumothorax versus pulmonary embolism.
rows.boundary: A gold-label flip alone does not establish a comparison; candidates may coexist and need not be mutually exclusive.

rows.name: Consequence derivation
rows.criterion: A changed premise leads through a supported relationship to an outcome that the current input does not already provide.
rows.example: Reason about HDL under the counterfactual that fenofibrate had never been taken.
rows.boundary: This is a taxonomy example only: M05 LabTest is not in formal v5. Formal v5 R4 consists of 13 HIV treatment scenarios. Repeating an edited fact or naming a Complication field is insufficient.

rows.name: Target invariance
rows.criterion: A specified judgment should remain under an actual input change, with a target-specific irrelevance or task-contract basis.
rows.example: Ethnicity changes while chemotherapy and ototoxicity evidence remain, leaving the queried drug mechanism unchanged.
rows.boundary: Equal gold labels or equal model answers alone do not establish invariance; demographic variables can be relevant to other targets.

sampling_design.actual_design: Preserve full annotation archive and all eligible R1–R4 targets; sample 450 unique eligible R5 units without replacement independently in each of eight sources.
sampling_design.choice_justification: Equal source-level R5 coverage under a practical comparison budget, approved after explicit proportional/equal-allocation discussion. Not a power-optimized or clinically representative sample.
rejected_not_executed: Whole-source removal preview retaining only DiversityMedQA R5; would reduce 38,123 to 7,611 units.

v3_overlap.caution: Not-in-v3 is not never-exposed. Earlier generation, source review and related versions matter.

sampling_design.dependencies: Sampling is by source unit, not by independent patient/root. Several strata contain multiple variants of the same root; selected source roots vary from 133 to 450. Equal units also does not mean equal child targets; unit-level aggregation prevents sources with many children dominating ALL.

reference_quality_boundaries.finding: R1 compatible-support classification does not independently establish a unique clinical diagnosis; six Bronchitis pairs matched author text/gold exactly but clinical exclusivity was not validated.

Point-estimate versus significance criteria and exact outcome binding vary across examples; author-reference agreement is not automatically causal or evidential correctness. Question families can share original_review and clinical studies.

All 13 formal R4 cases originate in author LLM-generated scenarios. Later acquisition confirmed six experts rated entire question/answer/explanation quality (20 CF × 6 ratings); there is no independently chosen expert binary reference. Do not incorrectly say no expert ever reviewed them.

Perturbed demonstrations are distinct from current premise/hypothesis evidence; source labels may contain support-scope or generation artifacts. Later diagnostic and training audits do not alter frozen v5 or license a blanket unreliable-label claim.
Several sources derive from MedQA; question groups/reviews/premises are not independent clinical patients. Deduplication and exposure claims must state the compared identities and exact scope.

supported_english: We organize medical counterfactual evaluation around five judgment-level functions: acquiring support, withdrawing support, reconsidering candidates, deriving consequences, and preserving a target under irrelevant change.

We curate an auditable evaluation suite from 11 sources, selecting 6,104 comparison units and 13,000 judgment annotations from a provenance-tracked archive of 55,991 records across 15 acquired resources.
The benchmark preserves source-native tasks and evidence contracts, supports overlapping functional labels, and separates semantic classification from scoring eligibility.
We evaluate seven system configurations spanning six method families, exposing substantial weaknesses on support acquisition and candidate reconsideration under the frozen native-task metrics.
conditional: Use “collected and curated” for existing source data; use “constructed” for the taxonomy/annotation/qualification/sampling/input/protocol layer.
“Counterfactual benchmark” can encompass source-native perturbations and task-specific hypothetical relations, but not every record is an identifiable individual causal counterfactual.
Use seven systems/configurations, or seven evaluated methods with immediate configuration disclosure; there are six method families because M4/M5 are two MedRAG configurations.
unsupported_or_overstated: An exhaustive systematic literature review of all counterfactual medical benchmarks.
55,991 newly authored or clinically validated test questions.
All R1–R5 labels directly measure internal reasoning operations.
Seven distinct algorithms at identical backbone, corpus, format and compute.
v5 is an untouched independent test set for heads developed using its results.
All annotations have independent clinician consensus or all reference answers are clinically verified.

strongest_complete_evidence.main_motivation: Across all seven configurations, the best native-task accuracy is only 31.44% on R1 (n=2,866) and 30.42% on R3 (n=733). ALL ranges only 47.35–51.61%, while R5 spans 63.42–73.37%; aggregate success masks uneven performance across functions.
strongest_complete_evidence.full_range_table_reference: tables.baseline_ranges contains all 42 formal values, not selected favorable rows.
strongest_complete_evidence.interpretation: These are operationally defined functional subsets of heterogeneous native tasks. Source/task and category membership are correlated, so low scores motivate targeted diagnosis and controlled heads; they do not alone causally establish that a model failed a specific internal reasoning operation.
strongest_complete_evidence.rare_axes: R2 n=79 and R4 n=13 require exact denominators and cautious generalization. R4 should be called author-reference agreement when interpreting clinical significance.
strongest_complete_evidence.bridge_to_heads: Use the complete seven-system evaluation to identify failure patterns, then present the independent head studies/control evidence and finally the integrated five-agent CF-MoA as successive questions. Do not replace the broad benchmark study with only the later two MedRAG configurations.
